content:
sophie: Heads-up: support flagged a few customers where requests intended for v2 ended up on v1 during yesterday's quota enforcement window.
liam: Any concrete signal? logs, metrics?
sophie: Ops found a spike at 18:02 UTC, router returned THROTTLED then sticky-match chose v1. snippet in the logs:
```
[2025-04-11T18:02:12Z] req_id=xyz route=tenant/alpha variant=v2 status=THROTTLED fallback=tenant/alpha:v1 reason=RATE_CAP
[2025-04-11T18:02:12Z] decision=sticky_match -> selected=tenant/alpha:v1
```
anita: If sticky_match is higher precedence than fallback when reason==RATE_CAP that's a logic bug. We intended explicit fallback to win for capacity reasons.
drew: UX problem: customers only notice quality regression, no console indicator or alert. We should show a small incident banner and a counter in the route dashboard called "fallbacks (rate cap)".
sophie: Telemetry proposal: emit metric `route.fallback` with tags: route,tenant,from_variant,to_variant,reason,quota_window. Count every event; sample traces at 1/100 for perf.
liam: Also add a structured log field `fallback_decision=true` so we can backfill and alert. Keep tag cardinality low.
anita: Router change: flip precedence so that when reason==RATE_CAP we consult explicit fallback_variant first, then sticky. Also attach `fallback_reason=rate_cap`. Unit tests to cover both path.
drew: For console, show an inline link in the traffic timeline to sample examples; incident banner should suggest "Increase reserved capacity / request dedicated capacity / contact support". Keep copy short.
sophie: Action list: 1) anita -> PR to router precedence + unit tests (ETA: today). 2) liam -> metrics schema & metric name + dashboard tile (ETA: tomorrow). 3) drew -> console banner mock + copy (ETA: tomorrow AM). 4) support -> saved Intercom search for "v2 -> v1" tickets (owner: support, ETA: today).
liam: We should add a canary run: deploy change to prod-canary, enable a forced-ratecap shadow on 1% of traffic and validate `route.fallback` increments but no customer impact.
anita: I'll include a feature flag behind `router.fallback_precedence_fix` so we can roll back quickly.
drew: Also tie fallback metric to billing dashboard so customers can see quota triggers correlated to throttles. Without that correlation customers will open tickets asking why quality dropped.
sophie: ops-bot scheduled: deploy queued anita/router-fix -> canary at 2025-04-12T02:15:00Z.
liam: After canary, run a small smoke pipeline to check sample traces contain `fallback_decision` field and reason tag.
anita: Will add those smoke checks to CI.
drew: Thanks. I'll prepare the console mock and flag the product incident page.
sophie: Good work, everyone. We'll reconvene if canary shows anything odd.
